clue.text: Just after start of flap, raising alarm

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from flap

parts.note: just means rightful, lawful or deserved

explanation.surface: Someone panics the moment a flap begins and sounds the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just after' reads like a time phrase, but 'Just' is a synonym and 'after' places it behind F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful enough to cause fear is said to be raising alarm, a phrase describing the effect.

clue.text: Genus providing cover for gardener, originally

definitions.text: Genus providing cover for gardener, originally

parts.words: Genus providing cover for gardener, originally
parts.note: the first gardener, Adam, covered himself with a fig leaf, and the fig belongs to this plant genus

explanation.surface: A plant group once gave a gardener shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' points to Eden: Adam, the first gardener, wore a fig leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ficus is the botanical genus that includes the fig tree, whose leaf clothed Adam in Genesis.

clue.text: Popular style extracted from play

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
touch means a characteristic manner or style

explanation.surface: A fashionable approach is taken out of a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby the ball is in touch when it crosses the sideline and is out of play.
explanation.definitionFit: In ball games a ball over the touchline has left the field of play, so it is out of the game.

clue.text: Result of shooting individual eagle, almost certainly

definitions.text: Result of shooting individual eagle, almost certainly

parts.words: Result of shooting individual eagle, almost certainly
parts.note: reads like hunting a bird, but in golf one shot on a hole, usually a par three, scores two under par

explanation.surface: A hunter brings down a single eagle, almost for sure.
explanation.walkthrough: An eagle in golf is two under par; a single stroke on a par-three hole gives exactly that, and most such feats come on par threes.
explanation.definitionFit: Holing the ball with a single stroke on a par three scores two under par, which golfers call an eagle.

clue.text: Basic way to finance a crazy combination

parts.note: a fund is a pool of money, a means of financing something
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A simple method of paying for a mad scheme is proposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamental means forming the base or core, so it is a synonym of basic.

clue.text: Dog that's used for scientific research

definitions.meaning: short for a Labrador, a retriever breed
a laboratory, the place where experiments are done

explanation.surface: A dog is used in experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: It abbreviates both Labrador, the dog breed, and laboratory, the room for scientific work.

clue.text: Fruit giving foot soldiers vital energy

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for Light Infantry
chi is the Chinese term for the life force flowing through the body

explanation.surface: A fruit is offered to infantrymen as a source of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of lychee, a small sweet tropical fruit with a rough red skin.

clue.text: Good reason to record one maximum speed

parts.note: to log is to record
I is the Roman numeral for one
c is the symbol for the speed of light, the fastest possible

explanation.surface: A motorist justifies logging a top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: In physics c, the speed of light, is the universal speed limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reasoning is logic, so the phrase describes rational argument.

clue.text: Cover protecting hard work by engraver

indicators.note: protecting means the cover word wraps around the hard letter

parts.note: a casing is a protective cover
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A protective sleeve guards an engraver's demanding work.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing is the craft of engraving or embossing decorative patterns into metal.

clue.text: Elected officer, usually

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
a general is a high-ranking army officer

explanation.surface: An officer is normally voted in.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means as a rule or on the whole, a synonym of usually.

clue.text: Pet name for boy in European language

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet
Alan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a European language would call a boy affectionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet name' looks like one idea, a term of endearment, but splits into Pet and name for boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in Catalonia, Andorra and the Balearics is a Romance language of Europe.

clue.text: Theoretically, the first thing in major report

parts.note: major means large or big
a report is a loud noise like a bang or gunshot

explanation.surface: In principle, the leading item appears in an important report.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmological theory names the primordial explosion as the very first event in the universe's history.

clue.text: Arab US aid corrupted

indicators.note: something corrupted is spoilt or distorted, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arab official is accused of misusing American aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Saudi Arabia is an Arab, so the nationality stands for the broader people.

clue.text: Dependence of daughter, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in means the daughter's letter goes inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: diction is one's style of enunciation

explanation.surface: A father describes how his daughter's dependence shows, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom 'so to say', but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Addiction is a compulsive dependence on a substance or habit, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Contract stable worker for place of entertainment

parts.note: to draw in is to contract or shrink
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: Someone signs up a stable hand to work at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, an agreement, but it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room is a formal reception room where guests are entertained at home.

clue.text: Keep quiet about love note

indicators.note: about means the quiet word wraps around the letter for love

parts.note: sh is the command to keep quiet
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay silent about a love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa this is the fifth note of the scale, also spelt sol.

clue.text: Immobilised by weather, novelist finished book

parts.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist
a book is finished when bound in its covers

explanation.surface: A writer completes a book while stuck in bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Being snowbound means unable to travel because of heavy snowfall, so stuck due to the elements.

clue.text: Prima donna seen in bookshop erasing errors

indicators.note: seen in means the letters can be found running inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A diva is spotted in a bookshop correcting mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female vocalist in a company staging operas.

clue.text: Run away from highway, not prepared to die

indicators.note: away from means the run letter is removed from the highway word

parts.note: an interstate is a US highway
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone flees the motorway, unready to meet death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not prepared' means having made no will, the legal sense of dying without one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intestate dies without making a will, so they have not prepared for death legally.

clue.text: Hero showing bravery in more demanding situation

definitions.text: Hero showing bravery in more demanding situation

parts.words: Hero showing bravery in more demanding situation
parts.note: reads as praise for courage under pressure, but points to Dickens's workhouse boy who bravely asked for more gruel

explanation.surface: A protagonist proves courageous when circumstances grow tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous scene in Dickens has the orphan holding out his bowl and saying 'Please, sir, I want some more'; 'more demanding' is literally demanding more.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's title character is the hero who boldly requested a second helping in the workhouse.

clue.text: Sharp tool best used with diamonds

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
the pick of a group is the best

explanation.surface: A sharp instrument works best on diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice pick is a pointed hand tool for breaking up ice.

clue.text: Brother left with father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A brother has gone off with their father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, departed, but it is the abbreviation L placed after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Brother is used as a friendly address to a mate, so both mean a friend.

clue.text: Musician from an island, in place of orchestra

indicators.note: in means the island words go inside the place of the orchestra

parts.note: the pit is where an orchestra plays in a theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician from an island joins the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is a musician who plays the piano.

clue.text: Require surgery on limb? Good luck in the theatre!

definitions.meaning: literally fracturing a leg would need an operation
the actors' traditional wish before a performance, avoiding saying good luck

explanation.surface: An injured limb meets theatrical well-wishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors superstitiously wish each other success with this phrase, while literally it describes fracturing a limb.

clue.text: Old capital new capital has shifted to

indicators.note: has shifted means the letters of the modern capital are moved around

parts.note: Tokyo became Japan's capital in 1868

explanation.surface: The seat of power has moved from an old capital to a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto was the imperial capital of Japan for over a thousand years before Tokyo.

clue.text: New colonists moved through water, crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the swimming word goes over and around the river letter

parts.note: swam means moved through water

explanation.surface: Settlers swam across a river to reach their new home.
explanation.walkthrough: A swarm is a group of bees leaving the hive with a queen to found a new colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm of bees sets off with a queen to establish a fresh colony, so they are new colonists.

clue.text: Indigenous inhabitant negative American upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: nay is a negative, meaning no

explanation.surface: A native person is annoyed by a pessimistic American.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mayan belongs to the indigenous Maya people of Central America.

clue.text: Regular army's gear

definitions.meaning: regular in the sense of even, consistent, the same throughout
the standard dress worn by soldiers

explanation.surface: A soldier's standard kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means consistent throughout as an adjective, and as a noun it is standard military dress.

clue.text: Soldiers of the king -— and queen, for example!

definitions.meaning: ordinary soldiers are ..., as in officers and ...

definitions.text: the king -— and queen, for example
definitions.meaning: chess pieces such as the king and queen are ...

explanation.surface: The king's soldiers stand alongside the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers rank-and-file troops and also chess pieces, which include the king and queen.

clue.text: Obscureness of article in work referred to by unknown

indicators.note: in means the article sits inside the reference phrase

parts.note: op. cit., short for opere citato, means in the work already referred to
a is the indefinite article
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An academic complains that an article is obscure because it cites an unidentified source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'op. cit.' is the footnote abbreviation meaning in the work already cited.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity means lack of clarity, so it is the quality of being obscure.

clue.text: The look of a modern artistic style, say

indicators.note: say signals that a word spoken out loud gives the answer's sound

parts.note: Art Deco is an early twentieth-century design style

explanation.surface: Someone describes the appearance of a modern art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Dekko is British slang for a quick look, as in 'have a dekko'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dekko is British slang for a glance, so 'have a dekko' means take a look.

clue.text: Home's home — for a short time

definitions.text: Home's home — for a short time

parts.words: Home's home — for a short time
parts.note: Alec Douglas-Home was Prime Minister for only about a year, living briefly at the Downing Street residence

explanation.surface: Someone's house was theirs only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was British Prime Minister in 1963-64; 10 Downing Street is the official residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The London address of the Prime Minister's residence was Douglas-Home's dwelling during his brief premiership.
